dedupe_keys.name: tartu airport gnss jamming finnair suspension and dme approach estonia 2024

description: This operations and retrofit case shows how deliberate GNSS jamming in the Baltic region forced a change of navigation infrastructure at a regional airport. Tartu Airport in Estonia offered only a GPS-based approach, and in April 2024 two Finnair flights from Helsinki had to turn back because interference prevented them from landing. Finnair suspended its daily Tartu service from 29 April to 31 May 2024 so that an alternative could be put in place; from 23 May Estonian Air Navigation Services provided approaches based on ground distance measuring equipment (DME), which jamming does not affect, and flights resumed on 2 June 2024. Officials attributed the jamming to Russia, although no state was formally held responsible, and the European Union Aviation Safety Agency issued revised safety information bulletins in 2024 on GNSS outages, jamming and spoofing across the Baltic, Black Sea and Eastern Mediterranean. Coverage: one airport and its air service, April to June 2024, within wider Baltic interference since 2022. Format and access: free news reports and airport statements; EASA bulletin 2022-02R3 is free on the EASA website. Caveats: facts come from press and company statements, without flight data or an official investigation. Simulation uses: operations and control of transport when positioning is denied, hazard exposure of GNSS-only procedures to jamming, and resilience value of terrestrial backups. Related records: GPSJam maps the interference from aircraft reports, Jammertest studies receivers under jamming, and the US DOT complementary PNT demonstration tested backups.
